chunks: Even if we accept the reliability of the tradition that, 'he will rise after his demise,' it could mean that he will rise after his name will die and after he will be in hiding and will not be known, which is possible in the language. Our proof that the Imams are Twelve also disproves this claim. Besides, the followers of this creed have perished, and praise belongs to the Lord. Had they been righteous in their beliefs, they would not have perished.
ai.seo_question: How does the author refute the idea that Imam Hasan al-Askari physically rose after his death?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs linguistic flexibility (ijmal) to argue that 'rising' refers to the obscurity of Imam Hasan al-Askari's name rather than a physical ascension, aligning with the Shia understanding of the Hidden Imam. He reinforces this by citing the consensus of the Twelve Imams, noting that the proponents of the opposing view have vanished, which serves as a historical indicator of its falsehood. This argument underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of the Imamate through the eleventh and twelfth Imams, distinguishing it from other sects.
